newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis steady to higher.

text.p: Basis levels for dark northern spring wheat were steady to higher Wednesday, and U.S. grain dealers said part of the rise was due to logistical problems in shipping grain through the northern U.S. Plains.
Dealers said a recent blizzard had halted movement in some areas of North Dakota and Minnesota, and coming frigid temperatures will likely further delay rail movement.
"Some people loaded trains last week, but it's taking a while to get delivery," a Minnesota dealer said. "You can still buy wheat but that doesn't mean it's going to flow right away."
On the Minneapolis Trading Floor, basis for 14 percent spring wheat was steady to 10 cents higher.

USDA's Market News Service (MNS) said bids for 14 percent protein dark northern spring wheat for January delivery in Portland were four to five cents higher than Tuesday's noon bids. MNS attributed the rise in bids to higher Minneapolis March wheat futures and to rail transportation problems.

MNS also said daily bids for soft white wheat for January delivery in Portland were four cents higher than Tuesday's noon bids, supported by higher Chicago March wheat futures and by moderate to good exporter demand.
